vocab.notes: Vykat někomu. The polite default with adults you don't know.
Tykat někomu; tykat si: to say ty to each other.
Kafe is the everyday word; káva is the neutral, written one. Both are fine at work.
To a friend: to je od tebe milé.
Short for "if anything comes up". Very common at work.

dialogue.setting: Your first week. In the office kitchen you meet the head of finance, then a colleague from your own team.

lines.speaker: Paní Kovářová
lines.cs: Dobrý den. Vy jste ten nový kolega z [[Londýna|Londýn|gen|after-z]]?
lines.en: Hello. Are you the new colleague from London?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.cs: Ano, dobrý den. Jmenuju se Tom Baker.
lines.en: Yes, hello. My name is Tom Baker.

lines.speaker: Paní Kovářová
lines.cs: Těší mě, Kovářová. Vedu účetní [[oddělení|oddělení|acc|object]]. Jak se vám tu líbí?
lines.en: Nice to meet you, Kovářová. I run the accounts department. How do you like it here?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: A lot. Everyone here is nice.

lines.speaker: Paní Kovářová
lines.cs: To ráda slyším. Kdyby něco, přijďte za mnou.
lines.en: Glad to hear it. If you need anything, come and find me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.cs: Děkuju, to je od vás milé.
lines.en: Thank you, that's kind of you.

lines.speaker: Ondra
lines.cs: Čau, ty jsi Tom, ne? Já jsem Ondra, sedím vedle tebe.
lines.en: Hi, you're Tom, right? I'm Ondra, I sit next to you.

spoken.note: seš for jsi: very common in Prague speech.

exercises.prompt: How does Mrs Kovářová speak to Tom?
exercises.listen: Vy jste ten nový kolega z Londýna?

hints.explain: "Vy jste" is the polite vy form; ty would be "ty jsi".
She asks if he's the new colleague from London, using vy.

exercises.why: "Vy jste ten nový kolega z Londýna?" Are you the new colleague from London? Vy: polite.

exercises.prompt: How does Ondra speak to Tom?
exercises.listen: Čau, ty jsi Tom, ne? Já jsem Ondra.
options: He asks Tom to say ty

hints.explain: "Čau" and "ty jsi" are informal: ty. Polite would be "Dobrý den, vy jste…".

hints.wrong: He asks Tom to say ty
hints.explain: He just uses ty straight away; colleagues of the same age often do.

exercises.why: "Čau, ty jsi Tom, ne? Já jsem Ondra." Hi, you're Tom, right? I'm Ondra. Ty: informal.

exercises.prompt: Your new boss, on day one. **vy** or **ty**?

hints.explain: Not on day one: your boss gets vy until they offer ty.

exercises.why: Your boss gets vy, at least until they offer ty.

hints.explain: Saying vy to a child sounds like a joke: children get ty.

exercises.why: Children get ty. Saying vy to a child sounds like a joke.
With vy, the verb is 2nd person plural, even when you talk to one person: Odkud jste?

hints.explain: Jsi is the ty form. Paní Kovářová gets vy: Odkud jste?

exercises.why: With ty, the verb is 2nd person singular: Odkud jsi?

hints.explain: Jste is the vy form. Ondra already says ty to you, so: Odkud jsi?

exercises.prompt: Do you want a coffee? (to Ondra)
exercises.why: To someone you say ty to: Dáš si kafe? (or kávu).

hints.explain: Dáte si is the vy form. Ondra gets ty: Dáš si kafe?

exercises.prompt: Would you like a coffee? (to paní Kovářová)
exercises.why: To someone you say vy to: Dáte si kafe? (or kávu).

hints.explain: Dáš si is the ty form. To paní Kovářová, use vy: Dáte si kafe?

context.speaker: Paní Kovářová
context.en: If you need anything, come and find me.

exercises.prompt: Thank her and say that's kind of her.
exercises.why: To someone you say vy to: to je od vás milé.

hints.explain: Od tebe is ty. Paní Kovářová gets vy: od vás.

exercises.why: Ondra is addressed in the vocative: -a becomes -o, like Jana → Jano.
